The migration is complete for the application code.

**Changed files (12):**
- `packages/accounts/src/repo/session.js`
- `packages/accounts/src/admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`
- `packages/accounts/src/service/teamService.js`
- `packages/analytics/src/repo/cohort.js`
- `packages/billing/src/repo/refund.js`
- `packages/billing/src/service/couponService.js`
- `packages/catalog/src/repo/supplier.js`
- `packages/catalog/src/admin/variantAdmin.js`
- `packages/orders/src/repo/shipment.js`
- `packages/orders/src/service/returnService.js`
- `packages/support/src/repo/sla.js`
- `packages/support/src/admin/macroAdmin.js`

Each call changed from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`. The SQL strings and the parameter arrays stay the same. `node --check` passes on all files under `packages`. The repository has no package.json and no test runner, so I ran no tests.

**Left on the old call:** `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` (lines 9 and 13). The file header says that it is a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, and that an upgrade replaces the file and loses local edits. A fix must go upstream or into a wrapper. Tell me if you want that wrapper.

**Not touched:** `cache.query(...)` calls in the repo files. These use the cache handle, not the database handle.
